description: Editorial intent-to-canonical routing for beginner no-limit Texas Hold'em queries. Candidate questions, not user search terms or Search Console data.
source_of_truth: Existing _source/pages.json, published HTML canonicals and sitemap.xml, with a small qualitative public SERP sample. All proposed primary and support URLs are published before this turn.

definitions.primary: The preferred first-party answer for this reader's specific task. Different intents intentionally have different owners. One primary does not suppress other useful references.
definitions.support: An adjacent, narrower or broader public educational route; not a second claimed ranking target for the same exact task.
definitions.editorial_priority: Subjective usefulness of fixing reader pathways without measured keyword volumes.

external_context.limits: Public competitor examples illustrate distinct tasks, not a rank, paid keyword difficulty, volume, or proof of first-party impressions.

candidate_questions: How should I start learning Texas Hold'em as a complete beginner?

specific_policy.buyer_vs_learner: /poker/poker-books-and-courses/ owns choosing or evaluating materials. /books/how-to-play-no-limit-texas-holdem/ owns author-described title and direct author-supplied Amazon destination.
specific_policy.course_vs_reference: /poker/free-poker-learning-path/ owns step-by-step beginner learning. /poker/no-limit-holdem-guide/ owns complete integrated reference.
specific_policy.betting_vs_math: /poker/betting-and-pots/ owns actions, raise amounts and side pots. /poker/poker-math-reference/ owns explicit price, bluff and defense fraction lookups.
specific_policy.first_visit_vs_etiquette: /poker/getting-started/ owns first-session planning and costs. /poker/table-etiquette/ owns live table procedure.

site_changes_this_turn.intent: Enable book shoppers to reach existing free subject-specific guides without duplicating author book links or claiming rankings.
site_changes_this_turn.implementation: Replace one existing overview paragraph with concise five-destination question routing; no new page or Article URL; source/compiled output match.
